props.gloss_en: there is no mitzva in the Torah whose reward is stated beside it on which the resurrection of the dead does not depend
of honouring father and mother it is written: 'that your days may be long, and that it may be well with you' (Deut 5:16)
of shiluach haken it is written: 'that it may be well with you, and that you may prolong your days' (Deut 22:7)

a father told his son: climb the tower and bring me fledglings; he climbed, sent away the mother and took the young, and on his return fell and died -- where is this one's length of days, and where is his good?
'that your days may be long' -- in the world that is wholly long
'and that it may be well with you' -- in the world that is wholly good
a bad thought the Holy One, blessed be He, does not join to the deed
Rav Acha bar Yaakov: 'that I may take the house of Israel in their own heart' (Ezek 14:5) -- this is the thought of idolatry
this is what he meant: were there reward for mitzvot in this world, it would have availed him and shielded him from coming to such thought and harm; so there is no reward for mitzvot in this world
R' Elazar: agents of a mitzva are not harmed
R' Elazar: agents of a mitzva are not harmed on their way there
R' Elazar: ...nor on their way back
and a place where harm is established is different [the agents' protection does not hold there]
'and Samuel said: how can I go? if Saul hears of it he will kill me' (I Sam 16:2)
Rav Yosef: had Acher expounded this verse as R' Yaakov, his daughter's son, did, he would not have sinned
some say: he saw an incident like this one
and some say: he saw the tongue of R' Chutzpit the meturgeman lying in a dung heap
Acher: shall a mouth that brought forth pearls lick the dust?!
